title: Waves at boundaries
target: Describe reflection and transmission at a boundary.
criteria: Identify incident, reflected and transmitted waves.
Distinguish fixed-end from free-end pulse reflection.
Track energy without assuming equal amplitudes.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A pulse travels toward a boundary, then one pulse returns and another continues into a second medium. What is the returning pulse?
cpa.guide: Reflected waves travel back into the original medium.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A sound wave reaches a wall. Part passes through into the next room. What is that part called?
cpa.guide: Transmission carries energy beyond the boundary.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An upward displacement pulse reflects from an ideal fixed end of a rope. What returns?
options: A pulse that must double in height.
cpa.guide: At a fixed end, displacement reflection is inverted in the ideal model.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An upward rope pulse reflects from an ideal free end. What is its displacement orientation?
cpa.guide: An ideal free-end displacement reflection is not inverted.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An incident pulse carries 18 J. Reflected energy is 5 J and absorbed energy is 2 J. What is transmitted energy?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A boundary produces reflected and transmitted waves. Why is equal amplitude not automatically guaranteed?
options: Every boundary must absorb all energy.
Energy division and amplitude depend on the media and boundary conditions.
Conservation requires every outgoing amplitude to equal the incoming amplitude.
Amplitude is always the same as energy in joules.
cpa.guide: Reflection and transmission can have different amplitudes; amplitude and energy are distinct quantities.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
